text:
alex: Heads up — seeing a correlated spike in PCIe AER/link retrain errors hitting GPUs in us-west-2 and eu-central-1 since ~08:12 UTC. Grafana shows a ~7% usable-GPU capacity drop and increased pod evictions. https://grafana.internal/alerts/pcie-link-flap :eyes:
sam: Confirmed on rack-12/usw2. dmesg is full of link down/retrain and consequent device resets. sample logs:
```
[ 12345.678901] pcieport 0000:3b:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e3
[ 12346.123456] NVRM: GPU 0000:3c:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12346.123460] pcieport 0000:3b:00.0: Link down
[ 12346.123470] kernel: pcie link retrain
```
sam: nodes are flapping between Ready/NotReady and k8s is draining GPUs automatically.
chen: Autoscaler drained 42 GPUs across the two regions. We spilled to smaller instances and saw a token cost increase (~12% M/M). Any quick mitigation besides full rack maintenance?
priya: First-pass suspected causes: PCIe switch firmware regression, recent kernel/driver combo, or thermal-induced link flaps. Need to avoid a full replace if possible. Proposing: 1) identify top-affected pcie switches and cordon those racks, 2) apply temporary kernel AER suppression to stop noisy resets, 3) pull Dedicated pool capacity for 24h if traffic > SLO. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
alex: Plan for now: 1) Run a targeted node-scan to mark nodes with >500 AER events in last 1h then cordon/evacuate. Command we ran:
```
ssh admin@node-XXX sudo journalctl --no-pager -u kernel -o short | grep -i "AER\|link down" | wc -l
kubectl cordon node-XXX && kubectl drain node-XXX --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
alex: 2) Toggle temporary suppression so we stop thrashing control plane: we can boot affected nodes with kernel param pci=noaer (temporary) and monitor errors. This hides corrected errors but avoids resets. We'll only do this short-term.
ops-bot: autoscaler: DRain triggered: 42 GPUs drained across us-west-2/eu-central-1 at 08:27 UTC (policy: protect-control-plane).
vendor-bot: Vendor support chiming in — we see similar reports tied to PCIe switch firmware v1.2.3 under heavy multi-GPU sustained workloads. Recommend rolling back switch fw to v1.2.1 or apply hotfix v1.2.4 which fixes link retrain under lane-stress.
sam: Do we have a rollback path for switch fw? Some racks were updated last week. If rollback isn't immediate, we should stop heavy bandwidth jobs on those nodes (eg. distributed training) and disable NVLink peer-to-peer where possible.
chen: I'll open a CAPEX/ops request to pull 24h Dedicated pool capacity while we remediate — need finance ok. Estimating cost delta ~ $12k/day. @finance please ack. :money_with_wings:
priya: Immediate actions agreed: A) mark & cordon worst-offending racks, B) temporarily boot affected nodes with pci=noaer to reduce resets and stabilize pods, C) throttle distributed GPU jobs via scheduler QoS and a cluster-level taint for high-IO workloads, D) vendor to validate firmware rollback/hotfix. We'll schedule firmware updates in the 02:00-06:00 UTC maintenance window.
alex: I'll run the scan now and post node list. After cordoning we'll bring up Dedicated capacity and re-route critical traffic. Also enabling extra alerting for PCIe AER rate per rack.
priya: Long term: require firmware inventory and a preflight for switch fw + kernel driver compatibility tests in our CI before fleet upgrades. Add to roadmap.
vendor-bot: We'll prioritize a hotfix backport and provide a verification checklist for rollout. ETA for hotfix: 24-48h.
sam: Thanks — posting node list in #eng-infra-ops once scan completes. Will also prepare rollback playbook for fw and a do-not-upgrade checklist.
chen: Noting this for postmortem: link-flap pattern, correlated by firmware batch, cascade -> autoscaler overreaction. Need better damping in autoscaler to avoid large-scale draining for transient link noise.
priya: Agreed. We'll avoid full fleet-wide drifts and aim targeted racks + Dedicated buffer. Follow-ups: postmortem and action items assigned. :white_check_mark:
